title: Branch Misalignment
definition: A discrepancy between the state of the local repository and the remote repository, causing a difference in the branches.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Local and remote repositories (like the ones on your computer and GitHub) have different versions of a project, causing an issue when trying to merge them.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A situation where local and remote branches are not identical, due to uncommitted changes or unmerged commits, leading to difficulties in merging.
difficulty_levels.expert: A state where the local and remote branches diverge, often due to uncommitted changes or unpushed commits, necessitating resolution strategies such as merging, rebase, or creating a new branch to maintain repository integrity.

extra_fields.insight: The realization that local and remote repositories may become unsynchronized, causing difficulties when merging branches.
